newsitem.title: USA: U.S. refinery margins up on strong gasoline prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. refinery margins up on strong gasoline prices.

text.p: Long suffering U.S. refinery margins improved for the fourth consecutive week as gasoline prices mostly held their ground amid a selloff in crude oil.
Overall U.S. refining margins jumped to $4.31 a barrel, up 44 cents for the week ended Feb 15, according to Paul Ting, analyst with Salomon Brothers Inc.
The margin improvements were nationwide with the exception of California, where margins dipped modestly from the previous week's levels.
The gains were due largely to the fall in crude prices "not being offset by fall in gasoline prices," Ting said.
"There was a big jump in the spreads between gasoline and crude oil in February. That's what's been keeping them up." said Paulo Nery, senior consultant with Pace Consultants Inc in Houston.
The margin strength was also aided by widespread refinery shutdowns for maintenance on the Gulf Coast during February, Nery said.
Margins may continue to gain on the back of gasoline firmness in the coming weeks as efforts to build stocks ahead of the summer driving season begin to heat up, analysts said.

"I anticipate March being a little stronger. Seasonally, it is usually better," Nery said. He forecast crude oil prices would continue their bearish movement, with nearby prices on the NYMEX slipping to about $21.50 a barrel in March and $20.00 in April.
Ting also forecast a continued bullish move for margins based on expected brisk buying interest in spot gasoline markets in line with typical seasonal trends.
Other refined products, such as heating oil or residual, will meanwhile remain well supplied, keeping a lid on margin improvements on that portion of the barrel.
"I think we could sustain the gains with gasoline inventories still reasonably low," Ting said. "Gasoline is the one bright spot."
Ting said he calculated margins for wet barrels on the East Coast firmed to $3.51, up 10 cents from the previous week, while Midwest margins jumped 85 cents to $4.59.
Gulf Coast margins remained the weakest in the nation, gaining 38 cents to sit at $3.27, West Coast excluding California jumped 92 cents to $5.04, and Califronia levels slipped 4 cents to $8.06.
